questions.solution:
Each peak in the ECG is identified with a letter from P to T that corresponds to a specific electrical activity of the heart. There is one ventricular contraction during one heartbeat, as the heartbeat rate is equal to the pulse rate. Hence, QRS complex represents one complete pulse.

questions.q: In which disease does a symptom of acute chest pain appear due to enough oxygen not reaching the heart muscle?
questions.solution:
Disorders of the Circulatory system:

Angina (or Angina pectoris): Due to insufficient blood supply to heart muscles, a symptom of acute chest pain appears indicating decreased availability of oxygen to the heart muscles. It can occur in both sexes of any age but its occurrence increases with age.

Coronary Artery Disease (CAD): It is often referred to as atherosclerosis, affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle. In this condition, the lumen of arteries gradually becomes narrower due to the deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissues.

Heart failure: When the heart is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the needs of the body. It leads to the congestion of the lungs (one of the main symptoms) because of which it is also termed as congestive heart failure.

Cardiac arrest: When the heart stops beating.

Heart attack: When the heart muscles are suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply.

questions.q: Which antigen is responsible for erythroblastosis foetalis?
questions.solution:
Erythroblastosis foetalis: It is a case of Rh incompatibility (mismatching). If an Rh-ve pregnant mother is having a Rh+ve foetus, then Rh antigens of the foetus are not exposed to the Rh-ve blood of the mother in the first pregnancy because the two types of blood are well separated by the placenta. However, during the delivery of the first Rh+ve child, some amount of foetal blood is exposed to the maternal blood. In this condition, the mother starts preparing antibodies against Rh antigen in her blood. These antibodies from the mother (Rh-ve) can leak into the blood of the foetus (Rh+ve) during next Rh+ve pregnancies and destroy the foetal RBCs.

Symptoms: Severe anaemia, jaundice and even death. Prevention: Administration anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

Mitral valve has two fibrous non-muscular cusps.
questions.solution:
Human heart:
Location: In the thoracic cavity in between the two lungs and slightly tilted to the left.
Size: Size of a clenched fist.
The heart is covered by a protective double membranous bag: pericardium. It has pericardial fluid in between.
The heart has 4 chambers: 2 atria (small upper chambers) + 2 ventricles (larger lower chambers).
Inter-atrial septum: It is a thin, muscular wall separating the right and the left atria.
Inter-ventricular septum: It is a thick, muscular wall separating the left and the right ventricles.
Atrio-ventricular septum: It is a thick fibrous tissue separating the atrium and the ventricle of the same side. These are having an opening within through which the two chambers of the same side are interconnected. Such openings are guarded by valves (atrioventricular valves):
I. Tricuspid valve or TV (made up of 3 muscular flaps or cusps): between the right atrium and the right ventricle.
II. Bicuspid valve or Mitral valve or MV (made up of 2 muscular flaps or cusps): between the left atrium and the left ventricle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The normal range of thrombocytes in the blood is:
questions.solution: Thrombocytes or platelets are small corpuscles that help stop bleeding and form clots. A normal platelet count is between 150,000 and 350,000 per microlitre of blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Given below is the ECG of a normal human. Which one of its components in humans is correctly interpreted below?
options: Peak T - Initiation of total cardiac contraction
Peak P and Peak R together-Systolic and diastolic blood pressures
Peak P-Initiation of left atrial contraction only
questions.solution:
• P is the atrial systole contraction pulse.
  • QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization.
  • T is the recovery of the ventricles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following connections in the human heart is CORRECT?

I. Fossa ovalis connects the right atrium to the left atrium
II. Ligamentum arteriosum connects the aorta and pulmonary trunk
III. Coronary sinus connects coronary veins to the left atrium
IV. A pulmonary trunk connects the right ventricle to the lungs
questions.solution: Fossa ovalis is a depression found in the inter-atrial septum. It is formed by the fusion of foramen ovale present in the fetal heart which connects the right atrium to the left atrium. Ligamentum arteriosum connects the aorta and pulmonary trunk. It is formed by the obliteration of ductus arteriosus in the fetus. A pulmonary trunk connects the right ventricle to the lungs. Coronary sinus connects coronary veins to the right atrium and not to left atrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Deposition of fatty substance in the lining of arteries is termed as ________.
questions.solution: Atherosclerosis is the narrowing of arteries due to plaque buildup on the artery walls when the endothelium becomes damaged, allowing the harmful type of cholesterol to build up in the artery wall.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How many times does a molecule of urea have to pass through the heart in its journey from liver to kidney?
questions.solution: Urea produced by the liver will come out of the liver through a hepatic vein, then it will enter the heart through the inferior vena cava. From the heart, it will enter the lungs through pulmonary arteries. Urea will then return to the heart through pulmonary veins. It will then reach the renal artery through the aorta. In this process, urea passes through the heart twice.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If the stroke volume of an athlete is 100 ml and the heart beat rate is 82/min, what will be the cardiac output?
questions.solution:
Cardiac output (CO): It is the amount of blood that each ventricle pumps during one minute.

Cardiac output (CO) = Stroke volume (SV) × Heart beat rate (HR)

= 100 ml × 82/min.

= 8200 ml (8.2 litre).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: All the following options regarding blood transfusion is incorrect, except
options: The recipient plasma should not contain antigens against antibodies present in donor plasma.
The donor RBCs should not contain antibodies against an antigen in recipient plasma.
The recipient plasma should not contain antibodies against donor RBC antigens.
The recipient RBCs should not have antigens found on donor RBCs.
questions.solution: Blood transfusion means receiving blood into one's circulation intravenously. Antigens are present on the surface of erythrocytes (RBC), whereas antibodies are present in blood plasma. For example, a person with blood group B has surface antigen B on RBC's and antibodies to antigen A in its plasma. Hence, when RBCs are donated, the transfer of antibodies does not take place. However, as the RBCs of the donor have a surface antigen, it should be ensured that the recipient's plasma should not contain antibodies against the antigen on red blood capsules of the donor. Otherwise, if transfusion is made between incompatible donor and recipient, the reaction between the antigens on the donor's RBCs and antibody in the recipient plasma will produce clot and blocked capillaries.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct?
options: Blood = Serum + Formed elements + Clotting factors
questions.solution: Blood makes up about 8% of the human body weight. It contains erythrocytes, leucocytes, thrombocytes (platelets) and plasma. The volume percentage of all blood cells in the whole blood is about 45% in adults (hematocrit). The rest consists of liquid plasma (e.g., water, plasma proteins, electrolytes, etc.).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the function of lymph?
options: Return interstitial fluid back to the heart
Contain RBC, leukocytes and more proteins as compared
questions.solution: Lymph is the fluid that circulates throughout the lymphatic system. The lymph is formed when the interstitial fluid is collected through lymph capillaries. It is then transported through lymph vessels to lymph nodes before emptying ultimately into the right or the left subclavian vein, where it mixes back with blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
In the following table 'X' is formed by the division or branching of 'Y'. Which one is an exception?
 
  ‘X’ ‘Y’
A Arteriole Artery
B Capillary Arteriole
C Venule Vein
D Renal Artery Aorta
questions.solution: Aorta is the largest artery that comes out of the heart. It gives rise to various blood vessels going to individual organs. The renal artery is a branch of the aorta. Arteries enter organs and divide to form arterioles. Arterioles further divide to form capillaries. Capillaries unite to form venules. Venules join to form veins. Thus, venules are not branches but tributaries of veins.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: CAD stands for
questions.solution: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is characterized by hardening and loss of elasticity of the arteries.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If due to some injury the chordae tendinae of the tricuspid valve of the human heart is partially non-functional, what will be the immediate effect?
options: The flow of blood into the aorta will be slowed down.
The blood will tend to flow back into the left atrium.
The flow of blood into the pulmonary artery will be reduced.
questions.solution: Tricuspid valve is the valve in the heart between the right atrium and right ventricle. The valve opens to allow blood to flow from atrium into the ventricle. Thus if tricuspid valve is partially non-functional, then the flow of blood into the pulmonary artery will be reduced.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following condition arises in subsequent pregnancies after the first normal pregnancy?
questions.solution: Erythroblastosis fetalis classically results from Rh incompatibility, which may develop when a woman with Rh-negative blood is impregnated by a man with Rh-positive blood and conceives a fetus with Rh-positive blood, sometimes resulting in hemolysis. A mother who is Rh-negative may develop antibodies to an Rh-positive baby. If a small amount of the baby’s blood mixes with the mother's blood, which often happens in such situations, the mother's body may respond as if it is allergic to the baby. The mother's body may make antibodies to the Rh antigens in the baby’s blood. This means the mother has become sensitized and her antibodies may cross the placenta and attack the baby’s blood. Such an attack breaks down the foetus’s red blood cells, creating anaemia (a low number of red blood cells). This condition is called a hemolytic disease or hemolytic anaemia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Iron-free compound of haemoglobin is
questions.solution: Haemoglobin is a conjugated protein, which is made up of a protein called globin and a non-protein group haeme. Haeme is an iron (Fe<sup>2+</sup>)–porphyrin complex. A mammalian haemoglobin molecule is composed of four haeme molecules with four globin molecules.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following does not control heart beats?
questions.solution: Glossopharyngeal nerve controls the posterior part of mouth cavity; therefore, it does not control heart beats.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In humans, blood passes from the inferior vena cava to the diastolic right atrium of heart due to
options: Pushing open of the venous valves
Stimulation of the sino auricular node
The pressure difference between the inferior vena cava and atrium.
questions.solution: The action of the heart includes contractions and relaxations of the atria and ventricles. The contraction of the heart is called systole and relaxation is called diastole. The dynamics of blood flow in blood vessels are no exception and blood flows through the blood vessels along a pressure gradient, always moving from higher to lower pressure areas.  The movement is also facilitated due to the development of suction pull, as a result of the pressure difference between the inferior vena cava and right atrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the least and most abundant leucocytes in human blood, respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct ascending order of different leucocytes of blood is:
Basophils > Eosinophils > Monocytes > Lymphocytes > Neutrophils

Neutrophils are about 60%–65% of total WBCs, and are major phagocytic cells of blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about erythrocytes is false?
options: In the life cycle of a foetus, erythropoiesis takes place in both liver and bone marrow.
They maintain the viscosity of blood.
They maintain blood pH as they contain haemoglobin which acts as a buffer.
The total quantity of RBCs in a human male body is around 5.5 million.
questions.solution:
The erythrocytes or RBCs are cells of blood produced by the red bone marrow in adults and by the liver in the foetal stage. The liver also helps in destroying old and worn out RBCs. These cells contain the respiratory pigment haemglobin which acts as a buffer as it can bind to small amounts of acid in the blood, helping to remove that acid before it fluctuates the pH of blood. These RBCs also tend to aggregate thereby increasing the viscosity of blood.

However the quantity of RBCs in blood is approximately 5.5 million per cubic mm of blood i.e. in one tiny droplet of blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A person has cardiac output 5600ml/minute and stroke volume 70 ml. What would be the number of heartbeats in 2 minutes in this person?
questions.solution:
Cardiac Output = Stroke Volume x Heart beats/min

Heart beats/min = Cardiac Output/Stroke Volume  

= 5600 ml/70ml

= 80

Therefore, number of heart beats of this person in 2 minutes = 80 × 2 =160 .

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How does interstitial fluid or tissue fluid form?
options: By the leakage of fluid outside the blood vessels
By the absorption of fats into the intestinal villi.
By the filtration of blood across the kidney membrane.
questions.solution: As the blood passes through the capillaries in tissues, some water along with many small water-soluble substances move out into the spaces between the cells of tissues leaving the larger proteins and most of the formed elements in the blood vessels. This fluid released out is called the interstitial fluid or tissue fluid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The pressure with which we feel the artery hitting our finger when we measure pulse is
options: The sum of systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure
The product of systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure
The difference in systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure
The mean of systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure
questions.solution: The minimum pressure in the artery is diastolic blood pressure, which is 80mm Hg. The maximum pressure in the artery is systolic blood pressure, which is 120mm Hg. When the artery expands, it expands from the pressure of 80mm Hg to a pressure of 120mm Hg. Thus, the pressure with which we feel the artery hitting our finger is 120 - 80 = 40mm Hg. It is also called pulse pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: By an angiogram, it was analyzed that there is a restriction to the flow of blood in the blood vessels. Which of the following disease can arise due to such a medical condition?
options: Angina pectoris and coronary artery disease
questions.solution:
Coronary artery disease (CAD): It is often referred to as atherosclerosis. It affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle. In this condition, the lumen of arteries gradually becomes narrower due to the deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissues.

Angina (or Angina pectoris): Because of insufficient blood supply to heart muscles, a symptom of acute chest pain appears indicating decreased availability of oxygen to the heart muscles. It can occur in both sexes of any age but its occurrence increases with age.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the incorrect match with respect to disorder and their associated clinical condition.
options:
Disorder Associated clinical condition
Cardiac arrest When heart stops beating

Disorder Associated clinical condition
Heart attack When the heart muscle is suddenly damaged

Disorder Associated clinical condition
Heart failure When the heart is not pumping blood effectively

Disorder Associated clinical condition
 
Ischemic heart disease Causes due to deposition of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue, which makes the lumen of arteries narrower
questions.solution: Ischemic heart disease is characterised by discomfort and chest pain due to the lack of blood supply to the heart, especially in times of excitement or exertion when the heart requires a greater amount of blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The flat horizontal line in between the waves of ECG represents time when
options: there is no mechanical activity in the heart but there is electrical activity in the heart
there is no electrical activity in the heart but there is mechanical activity in the heart
there is no mechanical activity in the heart and there is no electrical activity in the heart
there is mechanical activity in the heart and there is electrical activity in the heart
questions.solution: Electrocardiogram ECG has P wave, QRS complex and T wave. The P wave is an upward wave and indicates atrial depolarisation, QRS complex indicates ventricular depolarization. T wave is an upward wave and indicates ventricular repolarisation. The flat horizontal line is called the isoelectric line. There is no electrical activity, but there will be mechanical activity. Example: ST segment indicates atrial contraction.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following four statements 1-4.

(1) The second heart sound is DUB, which is associated with the closure of bicuspid and tricuspid valves.
(2) The duration between consecutive second and first heart sound is 0.5 seconds in a cardiac cycle.
(3) The heartbeat of a human increase when the adrenaline hormone is injected into it.
(4) The atrial systole in a cardiac cycle increases the flow of blood into the respective ventricle by about 70%.

How many of the above statements are incorrect?
questions.solution: The second heart sound DUB is caused by the closure of the aortic valve and pulmonary valve at the end of ventricular systole or at the beginning of ventricular diastole. At the beginning of the atrial systole, about 70%–80% of the ventricles are normally filled; hence, during atrial contraction (atrial kick), the remaining 20%–30% gets filled.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cardiac pacemaker in a patient fails to function normally. The doctors find that an artificial pacemaker has to be grafted in him. It is likely that it will be grafted at the site of
questions.solution: SA node is the natural pacemaker located in the right upper corner of the right atrium. SA node initiates the cardiac impulse. So, artificial pacemaker will be grafted at the site of SA node.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are four statements (I–IV) regarding the human blood circulatory system.


(I)    In the treatment of angina pectoris, nitrous oxide and nitroglycerine are used.
(II)   Veins have thinner walls and broader lumen than arteries.
(III)  Artificial pacemakers are used in arrhythmia.

How many of the above are correct statements?
questions.solution: In the treatment of angina pectoris, nitrous oxide and nitroglycerine are recommended, and they are proved to be very effective. Veins have a thinner wall and larger lumen, while arteries have thicker walls and a smaller lumen. Pacemaker is a small artificial device placed in the chest or abdomen for controlling abnormal heart rhythms. This device is used to treat arrhythmias and uses electrical pulses to prompt the heart to beat at a normal rate.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Observe the diagram and state the false statement.
options: In this graph, -1, 0, +1, +2 are millivolts and 0, 0.2. 0.4,.... are seconds.
Wave 1 represents impulse generated by SA node.
Wave 5 represents ventricular depolarization which causes ventricular relaxation.
Waves 2, 3 and 4 represent spreading of impulse from AV node to Purkinje fibers
questions.solution: The electrocardiogram is a report generated depicting the electrical activities of the heart. It resembles a graph paper showing time in secs on the X axis and current in millivolt on the Y axis. The wave 1 is the P wave which indicates the current generated from the SA node going towards both the atria and the AV node. The P wave represents the electrical activity - atrial depolarization and the segment PQ indicates the muscular activity of atrial contraction. The waves 2, 3 & 4 are called the Q,R,S waves which represent the electrical activity - ventricular depolarization indicating that the current moves from the AV Node to the Bundle of His to the Purkinje fibers. The ST segment after that represents the muscular activity of ventricular contraction. The wave 5 is the 'T' wave which represents the electrical activity - ventricular repolarization. The segment after that indicates the muscular activity of ventricular relaxation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following blood plasma proteins is correctly matched with its function?
options: Albumin : Maintain water level and osmolarity of blood
Globulin : Helps to provide antibody mediated immunity  <math><mo>(</mo><mtext>AMI</mtext><mo>)</mo></math>
Fibrinogen : Helps in coagulation of blood.
questions.solution:
There are three main types of plasma proteins:
  • Albumin: It retains water level in plasma, therefore, maintains osmolarity.
  • Globulin: It is the protein of plasma as antibodies or immunoglobulin molecules that provide AMI.
  • Fibrinogen: This plasma protein is converted into fibrin threads by thrombin enzyme at the time of blood coagulation/clotting.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the artery,
options: systolic blood pressure is lesser than diastolic blood pressure
the duration of systolic blood pressure is greater than the duration of diastolic blood pressure
the duration of systolic blood pressure is lesser than the duration of diastolic blood pressure
the duration of systolic blood pressure is same as the duration of diastolic blood pressure
questions.solution: The maximum pressure exerted by blood on the walls of arteries when the heart contracts is called Systolic blood pressure. Its value is 120 mm Hg. The minimum pressure exerted by blood on the walls of arteries when the heart relaxes is called Diastolic blood pressure. Its value is 80 mm Hg. Systolic blood pressure in arteries is due to ventricular systole which lasts for 0.3 seconds while the diastolic blood pressure in arteries is due to ventricular diastole which lasts for 0.5 seconds.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structure in the normal human heart generates action potential to initiate a cardiac cycle?
questions.solution: The SA node (sino-atrial node) is a specialised nodal cardiac tissue which is present in the right upper corner of right atrium. It can generate the maximum number of actionpotentials i.e.70-75 per min, and is responsible for initiating and maintaining rhythmic contractile activity of the heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements (A-D)
A. Coronary Artery Disease is also called atherosclerosis that affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle.
B. The electrocardiograph machine is used to obtain an electrocardiogram (ECG) on graph paper.
C. During a cardiac cycle, the right ventricle pumps out about 70ml of oxygenated blood which is called stroke volume.
D. The second heart sound is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves.
How many statements from the above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution: Right side of human heart contain deoxygenated blood and left side of human heart contain oxygenated blood so in each cardiac cycle the right ventricle pumps out about 70 ml deoxygenated blood while left ventricle pumps out 70 ml oxygenated blood to respective blood vessels.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Systolic blood pressure of a patient was 140 mm Hg while his diastolic blood pressure is 90 mm Hg. If this is not controlled, it can lead to

a Heart disease

b Brain haemorrhage

c Damage of the blood vessels of kidney

d Failure in conducting system
options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math>  and  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></math>
questions.solution: Blood pressure is the lateral force exerted by the volume of blood on the walls of the blood vessels. The blood pressure is high in the arterial circulation than venous. Normal ideal blood pressure in humans is 120/80 mmHg. When this pressure increases it signifies that the force exerted on the vessel walls is higher than usual and also the heart is pumping blood with much higher force than normal. This abnormal pressure if continued for a long duration will eventually lead to damage to the layers of the arterial walls which lose their elastic property and become hardened, the blood vessels of the kidney (Renal artery) being the most commonly affected. Also, high pressure can lead to the rupture of delicate vessels in the brain leading to brain hemorrhage. This continuous overwork of pumping blood with more pressure will lead to diseases of the heart too. The conducting system is not dependent on the circulation but instead dependent on the electrical circuit of the heart which is not affected by the raised blood pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Cardiac output is defined as the amount of blood
options: Pumped by the left atrium per hour
Received by the heart in one minute
Pumped by each ventricle per minute
Pumped by both ventricles per second
questions.solution: The ventricle pumps blood outside into the circulation. Each ventricle pumps out around 70 mL of blood in each cardiac cycle. This is called the stroke volume. Heart rate is the number of times the heart beats per minute or in other words the number of times a cardiac cycle occurs in a minute. Thus the stroke volume (the volume pumped out by each ventricle in one cardiac cycle) multiplied by heart rate (the number of cardiac cycles occurring in a minute) gives us the cardiac output. Thus the cardiac output is the amount of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute. It is around 5 L or 5000 mL in a healthy individual.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The arteries differ from veins in having:
options: Arteries consist of three distinct layers, which are thin and collapsible whereas veins consist of three distinct layers, which are rigid, thicker and highly muscular.
Veins consist of three distinct layers, which are thin and collapsible whereas arteries consist of three distinct layers, which are rigid, thicker and highly muscular.
Veins consist of two distinct layers, which are thick and collapsible whereas arteries consist of three distinct layers, which are rigid, thicker and highly muscular.
Arteries consist of two distinct layers, which are thin and muscular whereas veins consist of three distinct layers, which are rigid, thicker and highly vascular.
questions.solution: The pulmonary artery carries dark-red deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs whereas Pulmonary vein carries bright-red oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. ​Veins consist of three distinct layers, which are thin and collapsible whereas arteries consist of three distinct layers, which are rigid, thicker and highly muscular.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements (A-C) about the human heart:

questions.solution:
AV node is specialised mass of cardiac tissue present in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the AV septum.
The body has ability to alter the stroke volume as well as the heart rate and thereby the cardiac output.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is true about earthworm, scorpion, cockroach, and silverfish?
options: They all belong to the same phylum
They all have joined paired appendages
questions.solution: Earthworm belonging to phylum Annelida, scorpion, silverfish, and cockroach (belonging to phylum Arthropoda) all have dorsal heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The most active phagocytic white blood cells are:
questions.solution: The most active phagocytic white blood cells are neutrophils and monocytes. Neutrophil is a type of WBC (leukocyte) that has a lobed nucleus and granular cytoplasm. Neutrophils engulf bacteria and release various substance such as lysozyme and oxidizing agents. Monocyte is the largest form of WBC in vertebrates. It has a kidney shaped nucleus and is actively phagocytic, ingesting bacteria and cells debris.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding tricuspid valve
options: It guards the opening between right atrium and right ventricle
questions.solution:
It prevents blood from flowing back into the right atrium during contraction of the ventricle.

The tricuspid valve is one of the two main valves on the right side of your heart. Normally, the tricuspid valve has three flaps (leaflets) that open and close, allowing blood to flow from the right atrium to the right ventricle in your heart and preventing blood from flowing backward.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Pericardium is
questions.solution: The pericardium is a tough double-layered fibro serous sac which covers the heart. The space between the two layers of the serous pericardium, the pericardial cavity, is filled with serous fluid which protects the heart from any kind of external jerk or shock.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the option with the correct labeling.
options:
1. epithelial tissue
2. smooth muscle
3. connective tissue
4. valve
5. capillaries

1. smooth muscle
2. epithelial tissue
3. connective tissue
4. valve
​5. capillaries

1. connective tissue
2. smooth muscle
3. epithelial tissue
4. valve
5. capillaries

2. connective tissue
3. epithelial tissue
4. valve

questions.solution:
Arteries carry blood away from the heart, where it branches into even smaller vessels called arterioles and further branches into small capillaries, where the exchange of nutrients and other waste molecules occurs.

Veins carry blood away towards the heart, where it branches into even smaller vessels called venules and further branches into small capillaries. Compared to arteries, veins are thin-walled.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The correct arrangement of cardiac valves from the right side to the left sides is
options: bicuspid valve - pulmonary semilunar valve - aortic semilunar valve - tricuspid valve
tricuspid valve - aortic semilunar valve - pulmonary semilunar valve - bicuspid valve
tricuspid valve  - bicuspid valve - pulmonary semilunar valve - aortic semilunar valve
tricuspid valve - pulmonary semilunar valve - aortic semilunar valve - bicuspid valve
questions.solution: The valve present on the extreme right is the right atrioventricular valve also called the tricuspid valve it has three cusps. Just besides this valve, the right ventricle opens into the pulmonary trun and this opening is guarded by a pulmonary semilunar valve. To the left of this valve, the left semilunar valve guards the opening between left ventricle and aorta. The valve present on the extreme left is the left atrioventricular valve also called the bicuspid valve it has two cusps.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: State which of these statements about blood groups (ABO system and Rh system taken together) is correct.
options: The blood group having all the possible antigens present in these two systems is the universal recipient
The blood group considered as the universal donor is also the commonest blood group in humans
The blood group considered as the universal recipient is also the rarest blood group in humans
The blood group having no antibodies against any of the antigens in these two systems is the universal donor
questions.solution: Universal donor: O Rh-ve, Commonest blood group in humans: O Rh+ve. Universal recipient: AB Rh+ve, Rarest blood group in humans: AB Rh-ve. The possible antigens considering ABO system and Rh system are Antigen A, Antigen B and Antigen Rh. A blood group having all the three antigens is AB Rh+ve and it is the universal recipient. questions.solution:
The first deflection is the P wave linked with right and left atrial depolarization. A wave of which is invisible because of low amplitude.
The normal P wave is no higher than 2.5 mm (two-and-a half1-mm-divisions) tall and less than 120 ms (three 1-mm-divisions) in width in any lead.
The second wave is the QRS complex. The complex has a series of 3 deflections that reflects current associated with right and left ventricular depolarization. By convention, the first deflection in the complex, if negative, is called a Q wave. The first positive deflection in the complex is called an R wave. A negative deflection after an R wave is called an S wave. The most labile wave in the ECG is the T wave, which changes including low-amplitude T waves and abnormally inverted T waves, which may be the result of many cardiac and non-cardiac conditions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: There is no DNA in
questions.solution: Red blood cells are the most common type of blood cell and delivering oxygen to the body tissues via the blood. There is no DNA in mature RBC. The reticulocyte is the immediate precursor of the mature RBC and, within 24 hours of release into the peripheral circulation, evolves into the mature RBC and losses its nucleus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A volume of a healthy human blood is
questions.solution: Through various techniques such as injecting a harmless opaque substance of specific quantity and noting its degree of dilution, the blood volume in adult human body is measured to be near about 5 litres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following substances, if introduced into the blood stream, would cause coagulation of blood at the site of its introduction?
questions.solution:
Fibrinogen, prothrombin, thromboplastin are respectively clotting factors I, II and III.
Thromboplastin released from injured platelets or injured tissue. This converts prothrombin into thrombin in the presence of calcium ions. The thrombin converts fibrinogen into fibrin and the latter froms the clot.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The diagram below shows how things get to and from the liver. They are labeled as A, B, C, D, E and F. Which one of the following labellings is the correct one?
options: A is the hepatic portal vein and E is the hepatic vein
C is the intestine and F is the hepatic portal vein
D is the hepatic portal vein and F is hepatic vein
B is the pancreatic artery and E is the hepatic artery
questions.solution: The hepatic portal vein transports blood high on glucose concentration and amino acids from the small intestine to the liver while the hepatic vein transports deoxygenated blood from the liver to the heart and remaining glucose and amino acids to the rest of the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A person having which of these blood groups is surely homozygous?
questions.solution: Rh antigen follows normal Mendelian inheritance. If 'R' is the allele that produces Rhesus antigen and 'r' is the allele which doesn't, then a person with Rh+ve blood group can be RR or Rr while a person with Rh-ve blood group will always be rr (always homozygous). A person with A blood group may have genotype IaIa or IaIo. A person with AB blood group has genotype IaIb. A person with blood group O has genotype IoIo (always homozygous).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct events of a cardiac cycle beginning from the firing of an impulse from the pacemaker of the heart?
questions.solution: When the SA node fires impulse, it reaches the atria and they contract for <math><mn>0.1</mn></math> sec. During this interval, the impulse has not reached the ventricles so they are still relaxing. After <math><mn>0.1</mn></math> seconds, the impulse reaches the ventricles and they contract for <math><mn>0.3</mn></math> seconds. Atria are now relaxing during this phase. After this ventricles will relax. Thus the correct graph is C

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is different from others in the absence of a muscular coat?
questions.solution: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels in the body. Capillary has no muscular wall. Its, wall is made of a single layer of flat endothelial cells and is consequently very permeable-to water and small- solutes, but not to proteins and other macromolecules. The diameter of lumen of capillaries is from 7.5 µm to 75 µm. Only about 5 to 7% of the total volume of blood is contained in the capillaries.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following system returns the blood from the intestine to the liver?
questions.solution: Hepatic portal system is the system of veins comprising the hepatic portal vein and its tributaries. The portal venous system is responsible for directing blood from parts of the gastrointestinal tract to the liver. Substances absorbed in the small intestine travel first to the liver for processing before continuing to the heart. Not all of the gastrointestinal tract is part of this system. The system extends from about the lower portion of the esophagus to the upper part of the anal canal. It also includes venous drainage from the spleen and pancreas.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The matrix of blood is known as
questions.solution: Blood is a connective tissue that has a fluid matrix, called plasma, and no fibers. The extracellular matrix, called plasma, makes blood unique among all connective tissues because it is fluid. This fluid, which is mostly water, perpetually suspends the formed elements and enables them to circulate throughout the body within the cardiovascular system.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The atrium and ventricle of the same side is separated by
questions.solution: The atria and ventricles are separated by the atrioventricular valves. The tricuspid valve separates the right chambers, and mitral valve separates the left chambers. The atrioventricular septum is a thick fibrous tissue that ​separates the atrium and the ventricle of the same side.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per cardiac cycle is called <math><mtext>____X_____</mtext></math> which is about <math><mtext>_____Y_____</mtext></math> . Select the correct option for <math><mtext>X and Y</mtext></math> .
options: X- Stroke Volume; <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>70</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math>
X- Cardiac output; <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>50</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math>
X- Isovolumetric Systole;  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>50</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math>
X- Isovolumetric Diastole;  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>30</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math>
questions.solution:
The volume of blood pumped from the heart (left ventricle) into the systemic aorta in one minute is called the cardiac output. It is also called minute volume. It is calculated as the product of stroke volume (amount of blood pumped by left ventricle each time it contracts) and rate of heartbeat, i.e.,
Cardiac output = Stroke volume x Rate of heart beat = 70 ml x 75 times/minute = 5250 ml/minute or 5.25 litres/minute.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following terms doesn't mean one and the same?
questions.solution: The increase in the number of erythrocytes or RBCs is called erythrocytosis or polycythaemia. Monocyte are also called scavenger leucocytes since they can remove cellular debris. The left atrio-ventricular valve has two cusps and hence it is called biscuspid valve. It is also called mitral valve. Myocardial infarction is death of cardiac muscles while myocardial ischaemia is reduced blood supply to cardiac muscle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5 L, blood volume in the ventricles at the end of diastole is 100 mL and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 mL?
questions.solution:
CO = HR X (EDV-ESV) (Cardiac Output = Heart rate x stroke volume; stroke volume = End Diastole volume - End Systole volume);
We have, CO = 5 Liters,5000ml
EDV = 100ml
ESV =50 ml
Hence, CO = HR x (EDV - ESV)
HR = CO / (EDV - ESV)
HR = 5000 / (100-50)
= 5000 /50
HR = 100 bpm

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structures help in the absorption of fats through lymph?
questions.solution: Lymph is a colourless fluid containing specialised lymphocytes which are responsible for the immune responses of the body. Lymph is also an important carrier for nutrients, hormones, etc. Fats are absorbed through lymph in the lacteals present in the intestinal villi.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding blood pressure?
options: 90/110 mmHg may harm vital organs like brain and kidney
105/50 mmHg makes one very active
100/55 mmHg is considered an ideal blood pressure
150/90 mmHg is considered high and required treatment
questions.solution: Normal blood pressure in human is 120/80 mm Hg. 80mm Hg is the diastolic or resting pressure and 120 mm Hg is the systolic or pumping pressure. 140/90 mm Hg is high pressure than normal and requires treatment. Otherwise it may affect vital organ like kidney and brain. It is called hypertension.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Given below is the ECG of a normal human. Identify the right match of wave and its associated electrical activity.
options: Peak P and R: repolarisiation of atria
questions.solution:
P- wave represents depolarization of atria i.e contraction of atrial muscles which will distribute blood to ventricles.

QRS complex represents depolarization of ventricles to distribute blood.

T wave represents repolarisation of ventricles i.e. relaxation of ventricles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In humans, deoxygenated blood flows from:
options: Left auricle to left ventricle during auricular systole
Right auricle to right ventricle during atrial systole
Right ventricle to aorta during ventricular systole
Pulmonary vein to left auricle during auricular systole
questions.solution: The right and left atria are the top chambers of the heart and receive blood into the heart. The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from systemic circulation and the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary circulation.

(i) Blood through the pulmonary vein and vena cava enters in left and right atria respectively.
(ii) AVN generates action potential for ventricles.
(iii) SAN brings about atrial systole.

questions.solution: Blood through pulmonary vein and vena cava enters in left and right atria respectively and then atrial systole begins due to stimulation provided by SA node. Impulses from SA node will then be transferred to AV node which will bring about contraction of ventricular muscles which finally pushes blood away from heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If due to some injury, the chordae tendinae of the tricuspid valve of the human heart is partially non-functional, what will be the immediate effect?
options: The flow of blood into the aorta will be slowed down
The blood will tend to flow back into the left atrium
The flow of blood into the pulmonary artery will be reduced
questions.solution: If cordae tendinae of the tricuspid valve become partially non-functional due to injury then flow of blood into the pulmonary artery will be reduced.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: To which of the following, a bundle of His passes stimulus of contraction?
questions.solution: The waves of contraction originating from SA node, when reaches the AV node (pacesetter), the latter is stimulated and excitatory impulses are rapidly transmitted from it to all parts of the ventricle via bundle of His and Purkinje fibres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following waves of ECG are correctly paired with their events?
questions.solution: The graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart is called the electrocardiogram (ECG). A standard ECG consists of different waves which correspond to specific electrical event in the heart. First is the P wave which represents the excitation of the atria also known as depolarization of the atria. It leads to contraction of atria. The next is the QRS complex which signifies the depolarization of the ventricles leading to ventricular contraction. T wave corresponds to ventricular repolarisation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct statement regarding the tricuspid valve.
options: It guards the opening between left atrium and left ventricle
It is also called the mitral valve.
questions.solution:
It prevents blood from flowing back into the right atrium during contraction of the ventricle.

The tricuspid valve is one of the two main valves on the right side of your heart. Normally, the tricuspid valve has three flaps (leaflets) that open and close, allowing blood to flow from the right atrium to the right ventricle in your heart and preventing blood from flowing backward.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The pericardial fluid is present in the
questions.solution: The heart is enclosed in a fibrous sac termed the pericardium. The pericardium and its fluid lubricate the moving surfaces of the heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During each cardiac cycle, two prominent sounds are produced which can be easily heard through a stethoscope. The second heart sound is associated with:
questions.solution: Cardiac cycle is sequence of events cyclically repeated in the heart. This involves contraction of heart i.e. systole and relaxation of heart i.e. diastole of both atrias and ventricles. Two prominent heart sounds are heard during each cardiac cycle. These are Lub-Dub and can be easily heard with the help of sthethoscope. The first heart sound is lub or S1 and this is produced due to closure of atrio-ventricular valves i.e. bicuspid and tricuspid valves and is heard at the beginning of ventricular systole. Second heart sound is dub or S2 and this is due to closure of semilunar valves and is heard at the end of ventricular systole.

questions.subject: Zoology

AV node → SA node → Purkinje fibres → bundle of His → heart muscles
SA node → Purkinje fibres →  bundle of His → AV node → heart muscles
SA node → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres → heart muscles
questions.solution: The pulse making impulse travels in heart in the order of SA node → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres → heart muscles.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution:
The P wave represents the depolarization of the left and right atrium and also corresponds to atrial contraction.

The QRS complex represents the electrical impulse as it spreads through the ventricles and indicates ventricular depolarization.

T wave follows the QRS complex and indicates ventricular repolarization.

Stimulation of the sino atrial node
Pressure difference between the post caval and atrium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In electrocardiography, P-Q interval represent:
options: Conduction time through atria, A.V. node and rest of conducting tissues
questions.solution: ECG is Electrocardiogram. This represents electrical activity of the heart in graph format and is recorded by a machine known as Electro- cardiograph. This graph is obtained by connecting the patient to the machine by means of three limb leads and six chest leads. The ECG shows many peaks and each peak is denoted by an alphabet 'P' to 'T' referred as Waves. P wave marks the beginning of ECG and it denotes the conduction by Sino- Atrial node .P wave is followed by P-Q interval and this represents conduction through S.A node to AV node and rest of the conducting tissues.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The blood pressure values of four persons are given below

(i) Mr. A 120/80 mm Hg
(ii) Mr. B 80/120 mm Hg
(iii) Mrs. A 90/80 mm Hg
(iv) Mrs. B 150/80 mm Hg

Who among the following has normal blood pressure?
questions.solution: Hypertension is the term for blood pressure that is higher than normal (120/80). In this measurement 120 mm Hg (millimetres of mercury pressure) is the systolic, or pumping, pressure and 80 mm Hg is the diastolic, or resting, pressure. If repeated checks of blood pressure of an individual is 140/90 (140 over 90) or higher, it  shows hypertension. High blood pressure leads to heart diseases and also affects vital organs like brain and kidney.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not involved in the endocrine secretion?
questions.solution:
Endocrine glands are ductless glands as these glands pour their secretions i.e. hormones directly into the blood. Examples are pituitary gland, thyroid gland, parathyroid gland, adrenal gland, etc. Some glands are heterocrine glands as they have endocrine and exocrine cells both. Examples are gonads and pancreas. Hormones are secreted by cells of endocrine glands. Example, para- follicular cells or C cells of thyroid secrete Calcitonin. Similarly, Leydig cells of testes secrete testosterone hormones and Lutein cells of Corpus luteum (this is formed after the rupture of mature ovarian follicle) secretes progesterone.

Kupffer cells are the macrophages found in sinusoid of the liver.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The main collecting duct of the lymphatic system, the thoracic duct, receives lymph from the
options: left side of the head, neck, chest, left upper extremity and the left side of the body below the ribs
right side of the head, neck, chest, left upper extremity and the right side of body below the ribs
right side of head, neck, chest, left upper extremity and the entire body below the ribs
left side of the head, neck, chest, left upper extremity and the entire body below the ribs
questions.solution: As the blood passes through the capillaries some amount of it oozes out in the surrounding tissues. This is known as tissue fluid or interstitial fluid. When this fluid enters the lymphatic system it is known as lymph. Lymph is a colorless fluid as it lacks haemoglobin. It contains cells known as Lymphocytes which is important for immune system. The Lymphatic system consists of lymphatic capillaries, nodes, vessels and ducts. The lymphatic capillaries join to form lymphatic vessels. Large lymphatic vessels finally pour into one of the two principal vessels: Thoracic duct or Right Lymphatic duct. The thoracic duct receives lymph from the entire left side of the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the most abundant of all the cells found in the blood of humans?
questions.solution: Erythrocytes or RBC are the most abundant of all the cells in blood of human. On an average, the no. of different cells in a healthy adult human are: Erythrocytes/RBC: 5 millions to 5.5 millions per cubic mm. Platelets/Thrombocytes:  <math><mn>1.5</mn></math>  lakhs to  <math><mn>3.5</mn></math>  lakhs per cubic mm.Leucocytes/WBC: 6000 to 8000 per cubic mm.

It's closure is associated with the second heart sound (DUB).

The opening between left atrium and left ventricle is guarded by a valve formed of two muscular flaps or cusps called bicuspid or mitral valve.

Mitral valve is always associated with oxygenated blood of left side of heart and it's closure is related with first heart sound (LUB)

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What will happen to the body of an adult man if the spleen is removed?
options: Filtration of dead RBC will not be there
questions.solution: Spleen is the largest lymphatic organ. It is situated in the left side of abdomen region slightly above the stomach. It is considered as the 'blood bank' of the body. Histology of spleen shows presence of Red and White pulp. White pulp is associated with immune cells i.e. White blood cells. Red pulp consists of broken Red blood cells and also the breakdown products of Heamoglobin which is important as these gets metabolized to form bile pigments, urobilinogen, stercobilin etc. Hence Spleen is known as Graveyard of RBC. Red blood cells have a life span of about 120 days after which these die in the spleen. Splenic capillaries are smallest in diameter and thus when RBC's pass through them they die. Hence if Spleen is removed, this process will be hampered and also Haemoglobin metabolism will not take place.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The correct arrangement of blood cells is
options: In terms of quantity: erythrocytes > lymphocytes > monocytes > thrombocytes
In terms of life span: thrombocytes > erythrocytes > monocytes > lymphocytes
In terms of size: monocytes > lymphocytes > erythrocytes > thrombocytes
In terms of motility: erythrocytes > thrombocytes  > lymphocytes > monocytes
questions.solution: Blood consists of plasma and cells. Cells are formed elements. Agranulocytes are the largest in size. Monocytes and lymphocytes are agranulocytes. Platelets or thrombocytes are smallest in size.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Determine the wrong statement/s with respect to the nucleated blood cells.

I. The most abundant leucocyte is a granulocyte while the least abundant leucocyte is an agranulocyte.
II. The largest leucocyte is a granulocyte while the smallest leucocyte is an agranulocyte.
III. Phagocytic leucocytes may be agranulocyte or granulocyte.
IV. Polymorphonuclear leucocytes are the largest granulocyte while the largest agranulocyte has a kidney-shaped nucleus.
questions.solution: The most abundant leucocyte (neutrophil) is a granulocyte while the least abundant leucocyte (basophil) is also a granulocyte. The largest leucocyte (monocyte) is an agranulocyte while the smallest leucocyte (lymphocyte) is also an agranulocyte. Phagocytic leucocytes are neutrophils (granulocyte) and monocyte (agranulocyte). Polymorphonuclear leucocytes (neutrophils) are the largest granulocyte while the largest agranulocyte (monocyte) has a kidney shaped nucleus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A drop of each of the following is placed separately on four slides. Which of them will not coagulate?
options: Blood sample from the thoracic duct of lymphatic system
questions.solution: Blood serum is liquid minus clotting elements. It is of pale yellow colour. It does not have fibrinogen and other clotting materials. Thus, it does not take part in blood clotting.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Incorrect statements about the heart are

I. The sino-atrial node (SAN) is present in the right top corner of the right atrium
II. Ligamentum arteriosum connects the aorta and pulmonary trunk.
III. Purkinje fibres constitute a portion of the bundle of His.
IV. The pulmonary trunk connects the right ventricle to the lungs.
questions.solution: A patch of nodal tissue is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium called the sino-atrial node (SAN). Ligamentum arteriosum connects aorta and pulmonary trunk. It is formed by obliteration of ductus arteriosus in the foetus. A bundle of nodal fibres, atrioventricular bundle (AV bundle) continues from the AVN which passes through the atrio-ventricular septa to emerge on the top of the interventricular septum and immediately divides into a right and left bundle. These branches give rise to minute fibres throughout the ventricular musculature of the respective sides and are called purkinje fibres. These fibres alongwith right and left bundles are known as bundle of His.

questions.solution: As the blood passes through the capillaries some amount of it oozes out in the surrounding tissues. This is known as tissue fluid or interstitial fluid. When this fluid enters the lymphatic system it is known as lymph. Lymph is a colorless fluid as it lacks hemoglobin. It contains cells known as lymphocytes which is important for the immune system. The lymphatic system consists of lymphatic capillaries, nodes, vessels, and ducts. The lymphatic capillaries join to form lymphatic vessels. Large lymphatic vessels finally pour into one of the two principal vessels: Thoracic duct or right lymphatic duct. The thoracic duct receives lymph from the entire left side of the body. These two finally open into left and right sub-clavian veins.

questions.q: The CORRECT order of duration of various phases of the cardiac cycle is
options: Atrial systole < Ventricular systole < Joint diastole < Ventricular diastole < Atrial diastole
Atrial systole < Ventricular diastole < Joint diastole < Ventricular systole < Atrial diastole
Atrial diastole < Ventricular diastole < Joint diastole < Ventricular systole < Atrial systole
Joint diastole < Ventricular diastole < Atrial diastole <Atrial systole < Ventricular systole
questions.solution:
The action potential generated by the SA node stimulates both the atria to contract, which is known as the atrial systole. This action potential is then transmitted to the ventricles by the AV node and the Bundle of His, which makes the ventricular musculature to contract. Both the atria and ventricles then are in a state of relaxation called the joint diastole which is then followed by the ventricular relaxation, when the blood from the ventricles flow into the pulmonary artery and aorta. The aortic diastole takes place at the end of the cycle wherein the blood from the atria are pushed into the ventricles due to the opening of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves.

A rhythmic contraction and relaxation of heart during one heartbeat is called the cardiac cycle. The time required for one cardiac cycle is 0.8sec.

As SA node begins its conduction, the atria begin to contract, as a result of which the AV valves open and blood from atria enter the ventricles. questions.solution:
Rhesus factor, or Rh factor is a type of protein found on the surface membrane of RBC. This protein is genetically inherited where presence of protein is deemed as Rh+ and its absence as Rh-.

If a Rh- mother is impregnated with Rh+ father, there is a chance of Rh incompatibility as the baby will be Rh+. If the developing fetus is Rh+, the mother's blood will consider the Rh protein as foreign antigen and develop antibodies against it. Blood cells of mother will attack the baby as a defense mechanism which can be fatal. Such a condition resulting in death of baby is called erythroblastosis foetalis.

Blood flow can be precisely regulated in a closed circulatory system where blood flows inside the blood vessels. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system in which the blood pumped by the heart is always circulated through a closed network of blood vessels.
Open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs (except Cephalopoda) in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses. Mosquito is an arthropod hence it has open circulatory system.

Heart attack means when the heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an adequate blood supply. Heart block means when the action potential of heart beat is not passed to the ventricles properly. Cardiac arrest means when the heart stop beating at all.

The bicuspid valve is the valve in the heart between the left atrium and left ventricle. The valve opens to allow blood to flow from atrium into the ventricle. Thus if the bicuspid valve is partially non-functional, then the blood will flow back into the atrium and thus reducing flow of blood into the aorta.

questions.solution: Humans show double circulation. This includes two circuits: pulmonary and systemic. Pulmonary means blood from the heart enters the lungs and then back to the heart. It includes the right ventricle, lungs, and left auricle. Systemic circulation is blood from the heart enters the body systems and then back to the heart. The blood from the left ventricle enters the body through the aorta and this is oxygenated blood. The blood then returns back to the right auricle and this is deoxygenated blood.

options: Lub is a diastolic heart sound.
Lub occurs due to opening of semilunar valves
Dub can't be easily heard with a stethoscope.
Dub occurs due to closure of semilunar valves.
questions.solution: The cardiac cycle is a sequence of events cyclically repeated in the heart. This involves contraction of the heart i.e. systole and relaxation of the heart i.e. diastole of both atria and ventricles. Two prominent heart sounds are heard during each cardiac cycle. These are Lub-Dub and can be easily heard with the help of a stethoscope. The first heart sound is Lub or S1 and this is produced due to the closure of atrioventricular valves i.e. bicuspid and tricuspid valves and is heard at the beginning of ventricular systole. The second heart sound is Dub or S2 and this is due to the closure of semilunar valves and is heard at the end of ventricular systole.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which if these correctly describes the valves of the heart?
options: Bicuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve while the tricuspid valve is the left atrioventricular valve.
Bicuspid valve is the left atrioventricular valve while the tricuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve.
Bicuspid valve is the right atrioventricular valve while the mitral valve is the left atrioventricular valve.
Semilunar valve is the right atrioventricular valve while the tricuspid valve is the left atrioventricular valve.
questions.solution:
The valve present between the right atrium and right ventricle is the right atrioventricular valve also called the tricuspid valve as it has three cusps. It allows movement of deoxygenated blood from the right atrium to right ventricle but prevents the backflow of blood from the right ventricle.

The valve present between the left atrium and left ventricle is the left atrioventricular valve also called the bicuspid valve (mitral valve) as it has two cusps. It allows movement of oxygenated blood from the left atrium to left ventricle but prevents the backflow of blood from the left ventricle.

The opening of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk is guarded by a pulmonary semilunar valve. While the aortic semilunar valve guards the opening between left ventricle and aorta.
